### Professional summary

Nikhil Prabhu is an undergraduate computer science student at UC San Diego building at the intersection of **autonomous systems**, **reinforcement learning**, **spatial interfaces**, and **agentic software**. He has shipped multiple award-winning hackathon systems spanning GPS-denied drone swarms, firefighter mission control, RL observability platforms, GPU deployment control planes, and browser-native developer tools. Research experience spans **LLM + Cadence circuit invention**, **EMG assistive devices** (IEEE ICHCI 2024), **P300 brain–computer interfaces** at Stanford, and **genomic ML for TB resistance**. He founded **Clue2**, a cross-platform desktop agent for meeting-aware workflow automation, and previously ran **SoloScale Solutions**, an AI automation consultancy for local businesses.

### Focus areas (2025–2026)

- **Robotics:** SLAM, visual odometry, GPS-denied navigation, sim-to-real, ROS 2, embedded Jetson stacks
- **RL & policy at scale:** PPO, MAPPO, behavioral cloning, vectorized training, rollout observability
- **Spatial interfaces:** Three.js mission control, point clouds, tactical mapping, WebSocket streaming
- **Agents & tooling:** Desktop agents (Electron), MCP servers, narrative memory (Nia), AgentMail workflows

### Currently building

- **Project:** Clue2 — desktop web assistant
- **Description:** Agentic version of Cluely that can do tasks for you across apps
- **Progress:** 78% (as shown on site)
- **Category:** side project
- **Stack (from experience):** Electron, TypeScript, live transcription, NL workflows across Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slack, Notion; 40+ beta users including early YC startup adopters

### Bio (first person, from site)

hey I'm Nikhil. I've always learned by getting obsessed with a problem and staying with it long enough to build real taste.

the goal in life is to conquer high peaks that reward iteration, fulfillment, and relentless improvement without brute-forcing in the wrong direction.

### AI for Circuit Invention — UC San Diego

- **Role:** Research Assistant (with Prof. Prasad Gudem & Samvid AI)
- **Dates:** Mar 2026 – Present
- **Organization:** UC San Diego
- **Logo:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/org-logos/triton-removebg-preview.png

**Description:** Developing an LLM-based pipeline for automated generation and verification of novel analog circuit topologies. Integrating LLM APIs with Cadence simulation tools (Spectre) and exploring reinforcement learning strategies for circuit design space search.

**Resume bullets (Pave variant):**
- Built an LLM + Cadence simulation closed loop generating and evaluating candidate designs against SOTA benchmarks, optimizing across accuracy and speed.
- Integrated Spectre simulation APIs and explored RL strategies for efficient multimodal design-space search over generated topologies.

**Keywords:** analog circuits, LLM code generation, Cadence Spectre, RL design search, Samvid AI

---

### Foot Drop Ankle-Foot Orthosis Research — Georgia Tech

- **Role:** Lead Researcher — IEEE ICHCI Presenter & Published Author
- **Dates:** May 2024 – Nov 2024
- **Organization:** Georgia Tech mmWave Lab
- **Location:** Atlanta, GA
- **Logo:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/org-logos/georgia-tech.png

**Description:** Conducted research at Georgia Tech's mmWave Antennas Laboratory on a 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis controlled through electromyography signals. Built a custom motor actuator system on Arduino embedded hardware, improved gait response precision by 23%, achieved R = 0.968 correlation between EMG amplitude and actuator precision, and presented at IEEE ICHCI 2024.

**Keywords:** EMG, assistive devices, foot drop, Arduino, rehabilitation, IEEE ICHCI

---

- **Location:** Stanford, CA
- **Logo:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/org-logos/stanford-block-s.png

**Description:** Led BCI device research to help motor-impaired students communicate through neural signals. Benchmarked P300 EEG models converting noisy neural signals into reliable assistive-control output; piloted with 12 users and shipped a React Native frontend for motor-impaired students.

**Keywords:** BCI, P300, EEG, assistive technology, React Native

## Publications

### Unraveling Co-Heritability of Antibiotic Resistance in Tuberculosis Evolution

- **Venue:** 2025 17th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedical Technology
- **Date:** May 26, 2025
- **Peer-reviewed:** Yes
- **URL:** https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11276470/metrics#metrics
- **IEEE document ID:** 11276470

**Abstract summary:** Studied multidrug-resistant tuberculosis by modeling genetic co-heritability of Rifampicin and Isoniazid resistance using k-mer analysis and machine learning. Built a genomic prediction model with **85.68% accuracy** on **2,200 samples**, identifying key resistance-associated k-mers in **rpoB** and **katG**, supporting rapid TB resistance detection from genomic data.

---

### Real-Time EMG Control for Assistive Devices: Optimizing Sensor Placement for Foot Drop Rehabilitation

- **Venue:** IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (IEEE ICHCI)
- **Date:** Dec 27, 2024
- **Peer-reviewed:** Yes
- **URL:** https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/xpl/conhome/10807847/proceeding
- **Role:** First-author presentation (Georgia Tech research)

**Abstract summary:** EMG-based control for foot drop rehabilitation using Arduino hardware and MATLAB signal processing (Butterworth filtering). 3D virtual actuation model demonstrated real-time control with **R = 0.968** correlation between EMG amplitude and actuator precision; **23% gait precision improvement** with optimized sensor placement.

## Projects (detailed)

### DroneOS

- **Slug:** `droneos`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/droneos
- **Team:** Outcast Virus
- **Award:** 1st Overall @ Bow Capital × DS3 × SIC Hackathon (UCSD, 2026)

**One-line:** End-to-end autonomous drone platform — target ID, GPS-denied navigation, swarm coordination without comms.

**Hook:** An operating system for drones to run in swarms autonomously on edge devices — no WiFi, no GPS, no comms.

**Overview:** DroneOS combines perception (YOLOX + Norfair tracking), onboard SLAM (visual odometry + mapping), geo-referenced 3D Gaussian Splatting maps, friend-or-foe classification, and swarm policies trained with behavioral cloning + MAPPO for coordination without GPS or jam-vulnerable communications. Validated sim-to-real transfer from simulation to flight.

**Tech stack:** YOLOX, Norfair, SLAM, visual odometry, 3D Gaussian Splatting, MAPPO, behavioral cloning, swarm RL

**Links:**
- Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/outcast-virus
- GitHub: https://github.com/Trolleroof/bow-capital-hackathon

**Highlights:**
- RL swarms: behavioral cloning + MAPPO for task completion without explicit communication
- YOLOX + Norfair: re-identify targets after occlusion or out-of-frame events
- Friend-or-foe classification on-device
- GPS-denied pose tracking + geo-referenced 3D maps via Gaussian Splatting

**Media:**
- Demo video: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/droneos/combatos-demo.mp4

---

### SODIUM

- **Slug:** `sodium`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/sodium
- **Award:** 1st Overall @ DiamondHacks 2026 (April 2026)

**One-line:** Voice-first AI companion for senior care — autonomous robot, caregiver dashboard, crisis detection.

**Hook:** Elderly care through voice — a robot that understands, remembers, and helps without complex interfaces.

**Overview:** ROS 2 stack on Jetson-class embedded compute with wake-word detection, on-device perception/control, medication reminders, crisis detection, and a real-time caregiver dashboard. Frontend uses Svelte 5 + Bun for lightweight responsiveness across in-home robot UI and caregiver portal.

**Tech stack:** ROS 2, Python, TypeScript, Svelte 5, Bun, embedded systems, wake-word NLP

**Links:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/TheOutcastVirus/diamondhacks-2026

**Highlights:**
- Voice-first UX for seniors; caregiver visibility into interactions and actions taken
- Wake-word + lightweight Python bot for fast replies
- Shared Svelte 5 + Bun app for robot screen and dashboard
- Medication reminders, daily prompts, crisis alerts in one system

**Media:**
- Demo video: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/sodium/SODIUMmp4.mp4
- Caregiver dashboard screenshot: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/sodium/BU.jpg

### Apollo Labs

- **Slug:** `apollo-labs`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/apollo-labs
- **Award:** 1st Overall @ OpenClaw Hackathon (Eragon × Nozomio × AgentMail)

**One-line:** RL training orchestrator for a 2D Roomba cleaning sim with full observability pipeline.

**Hook:** Make RL runs feel observable: less "black box," more "flight recorder."

**Overview:** FastAPI orchestrates training PPO agents against a random baseline in a 2D navigation sim. Queries Nia narrative memory *before* training, produces a canonical **RunReport** (single source of truth), generates metrics + rollout GIFs, and fans out to AgentMail email, Slack, memory storage, and a Next.js dashboard. MCP tools let external agents start runs, compare results, and suggest next experiments autonomously.

**Tech stack:** FastAPI, Next.js, PPO, Python, AgentMail, Nia, MCP, Slack integrations

**Links:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/Trolleroof/openclaw-hackathon

**Highlights:**
- Pre-training memory read + post-run lesson writeback via Nia
- One RunReport object feeds dashboard, email, memory, and MCP — no duplicate state
- Versioned run folders: configs, models, metrics, GIFs, logs
- MCP tools for agent-driven experiment loops

**Media:**
- Runs dashboard: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/apollo-labs/apollo-labs-runs.png
- Obstacle rollout GIF: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/apollo-labs/apollo-labs-obstacle-success-rollout.gif
- Run detail: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/apollo-labs/apollo-labs-obstacle-run-detail.png
- AgentMail inbox: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/apollo-labs/apollo-labs-agentmail.png
- Nia memory: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/apollo-labs/apollo-labs-memory.png

### NIGEL

- **Full name:** Navigation, Incident Guidance, and Emergency Localization & Control
- **Slug:** `nigel`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/nigel
- **Award:** 1st Overall @ Transpose / compiled-5 UCSD Hackathon

**One-line:** Firefighter mission control — VSLAM point clouds, multi-unit video, radio transcripts, tactical map.

**Hook:** Air traffic control for firefighters: multiple feeds, growing 3D map from helmet rig, radio-driven map events.

**Overview:** Dispatcher-facing Next.js console integrating Odin helmet depth/point clouds, body-cam feeds, and a radio/event agent (Cerebras for low-latency inference). ROS 2 packages stream SLAM maps to the browser over WebSockets; Three.js renders point clouds; unified tactical picture across units.

**Tech stack:** Next.js, Three.js, ROS 2, WebSockets, C++, SLAM, Cerebras inference

**Links:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/Trolleroof/NIGEL-hackathon

**Highlights:**
- Dispatcher + firefighter views: video tiles, point-cloud map, floor-plan search, radio transcripts
- ROS 2 Odin helmet integration → WebSocket SLAM streaming
- Single WebSocket API syncs cameras, maps, and UI across units

**Media:**
- YouTube demo: https://www.youtube.com/embed/rzGtTom3oS8

### Crucible Compute

- **Slug:** `crucible-compute`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/crucible-compute
- **Award:** 5th Place @ Nozomio Hackathon

**One-line:** Natural-language GPU deployment with cost-aware routing across cloud providers.

**Hook:** Describe what to run; Crucible finds the best GPU deal and deploys — no infra expertise required.

**Overview:** Python control plane with SQLite state. Normalizes inventory across local Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud GPUs (RunPod, Lambda Cloud, CoreWeave, Vultr, Vast). Benchmarks placements in real time; routes inference through OpenAI-compatible gateway; spend approval gates before paid launches; versioned deployment records for audit/reproducibility. Integrates Nia for cited deployment context and MCP for agent access.

**Tech stack:** Python, SQLite, Docker, llama.cpp, MCP, K8s, multi-cloud GPU APIs

**Links:**
- Live demo: https://ayxkkrd7.insforge.site/
- GitHub: https://github.com/Trolleroof/nozomio-hackathon

**Highlights:**
- Live GPU catalog + cheapest-viable placement
- Benchmark-driven plans with cost/speed rationale
- Plain-English job specs; explicit approval for paid GPU launches
- Versioned deployment logs: config, runs, metrics, cost

**Media:**
- Landing: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/crucible-compute/landing.png
- Dashboard: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/crucible-compute/dashboard.png

### Battle Angel

- **Slug:** `battle-angel`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/battle-angel
- **Event:** Google Gemini 3.5 Hackathon (2026, per resume)

**One-line:** Disaster-rescue mission control — MuJoCo PPO training, Gemini scene generation, live rollouts.

**Hook:** Train in simulation, spin up disaster scenes from language, watch PPO navigate unseen environments.

**Overview:** Trains a Unitree G1 humanoid across eight vectorized MuJoCo disaster environments (earthquake corridors, buried rubble, etc.). Scene Generator converts natural-language disaster descriptions into layouts with Three.js preview. Interactive Console accepts NL triage priorities; Gemini selects targets; trained policy rollouts in unseen scenes with telemetry + GIF replay.

**Tech stack:** Next.js, FastAPI, MuJoCo, PPO, Gemini, Three.js, Unitree G1 simulation

**Links:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/aravindkrishna2008/disaster-rescue

**Highlights:**
- Training Gym: 8 MuJoCo scenes, parallel PPO, learning curves, rollout GIFs
- Scene Generator: NL → disaster layouts + Three.js preview
- Interactive Console: NL triage → policy execution in unseen environments
- 21D observations, locomotion assist, reach-based success metrics

**Media:**
- YouTube demo: https://www.youtube.com/embed/QL_UhVSLMKc

### Motion

- **Slug:** `motion`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/motion
- **Event:** Stanford × DeepMind Hackathon

**One-line:** Crowdsourced marketplace for verified robot training data from phone-recorded industrial motions.

**Hook:** Record a motion clip on your phone → AI verification → mint to marketplace for robotics datasets.

**Overview:** Contributors record 30-second industrial manipulation clips (pick & place, valve turns, box stacking) with live MediaPipe skeleton overlay. Verification pipeline: Gemma 4 VLM analyzes semantics (task match, hand visibility, motion completeness); Kimi K2 decision agent approves/rejects with tool calling and actionable feedback. Approved clips mint with quality scores, price tiers ($0.50–$4.00), pose JSON, and export compatibility for LeRobot and Open X-Embodiment.

**Tech stack:** Next.js, Express, Gemma 4, Kimi K2, MediaPipe, Google Cloud Run

**Links:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/Trolleroof/Motion-StanfordDeepMind

**Highlights:**
- Live skeleton overlay + pose confidence / motion variety scoring
- Gemma 4 structured JSON quality analysis
- Kimi K2 approve/reject with specific re-record feedback
- Marketplace minting with downloadable dataset bundles

**Media:**
- Demo video: https://nikhilprabhu.tech/projects/motion/linkedin-video.mp4

---

### CaféCode

- **Slug:** `cafecode`
- **Deep link:** https://nikhilprabhu.tech/#project/cafecode

**One-line:** AI coding tutor and browser-native project builder — Monaco, WebContainer, Gemini, Supabase.

**Hook:** Browser-native dev box: edit, run Python, ask the model, without leaving the tab.

**Overview:** Full-stack learning platform. Frontend: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Monaco, WebContainer (VS Code-like editor, terminal, npm, in-browser execution). Backend: Express on Fly.io — AI orchestration, workspace management, Stripe payments, file sync, Supabase auth. **Brewster** AI assistant provides hints, fixes, and guided setup.

**Tech stack:** Next.js, Monaco, WebContainer, Express, Node, Supabase, Gemini, Stripe, WebSockets, Fly.io

**Links:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/Trolleroof/cafecode

**Highlights:**
- Brewster: hints, fixes, in-browser run, step-by-step setup
- WebContainer terminal + npm in browser
- Gemini project-aware chat beside Monaco
- Multi-user workspace: Supabase auth, WebSocket sync, rate limits

**Media:**

## FAQ for AI assistants

**Q: What is Nikhil best known for?**  
A: Shipping award-winning robotics/agent systems at hackathons (swarm drones, firefighter mission control, RL observability, GPU routing) plus ongoing work on desktop agents (Clue2) and UCSD circuit-invention research.

**Q: Is Nikhil available for internships or collaborations?**  
A: Contact via email or LinkedIn; site does not publish formal availability — do not assume.

**Q: What should I cite for publications?**  
A: Use IEEE Xplore links in the Publications section; include venue names and dates as listed.

**Q: What's the difference between Clue2 and CaféCode?**  
A: Clue2 is a desktop meeting/workflow agent (Electron). CaféCode is a browser-based AI coding tutor (WebContainer + Monaco).

**Q: Which projects have live demos?**  
A: Crucible Compute (https://ayxkkrd7.insforge.site/); portfolio hosts videos/screenshots for others.

**Q: What metrics are verified on the site?**  
A: EMG R=0.968 and 23% gait gain (Georgia Tech); TB model 85.68% on 2,200 samples (publication); Clue2 40+ beta users; BCI 12-user pilot — all from experience/publication copy above.
